summary: Internal runner SSO session cookie path truncated, blocks elevated CLI commands
description:
Issue summary:
After the identity-proxy release v2.3.0, the session cookie used by the internal oncall runner CLI is being truncated to a shorter path (e.g. /api) which causes the runner to lose the web SSO session when attempting elevated commands.

Impact:
- On-call engineers cannot run elevated infra commands via the internal 'runner' CLI without being redirected to re-auth.
- Affects all environments in us-west where identity-proxy v2.3.0 is deployed.
- Interrupts incident response workflows; workarounds are non-obvious and increase time-to-resolution.

Environment:
- prod us-west cluster running identity-proxy v2.3.0 and oncall-runner 1.7.2
- Affected users are primarily SSO-authenticated employees on the enterprise org.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login to the web console as an SSO user (okta) and verify session is active.
2) On terminal, run: runner run --elevate --target=infra-node-01
3) CLI issues a request to /api/runner/elevate and receives a 302 redirect to /sso/authorize with query error=session_mismatch
4) Runner falls into reauth loop; no token is produced.

Observed logs / error messages:
- ingress-auth (identity-proxy) logs: "cookie path mismatch: expected='/' actual='/api'"
- runner CLI: "error: SSO session missing or invalid (status 302)"
- browser developer console: cookie set by identity-proxy has Path=/api and SameSite=Lax

Notes: This is not affecting basic web console sessions; only endpoints that rely on cookie path crossing between / and /api.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: recent cookie-path handling change in identity-proxy caused path to be set to request path instead of root.
Findings:
- Reproduced on staging by deploying identity-proxy v2.3.0; identical symptoms.
- identity-proxy change log shows commit that attempted to tighten cookie scope for API routes (commit 9b7c4f).
- Debugging identity-proxy session-store revealed a truncation in the cookie serializer when cookie metadata exceeded 128 bytes; path value fell back to request.Path which was '/api'.
- Okta SSO flow sends original redirect to /sso/callback which expects cookie with Path='/' to be attached to subsequent subrequests. With Path='/api' cookie is not presented for CLI elevation flows routed at /.
- Confirmed runner CLI works when identity-proxy downgraded to v2.2.9.
Evidence and links:
- identity-proxy logs: /var/log/identity-proxy/2026-02-28.log (lines with cookie-write events)
- Reproducer: staging cluster deployment rollout #2026-02-28-18:42
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/12890 (cookie scoping change)

Workarounds tested:
- runner login --web (opens browser flow and writes local token) — works for temporary access but not ideal for scripted runbooks.
- Manually setting REDWOOD_RUNNER_COOKIE_PATH=/ in identity-proxy env on a canary host — allowed normal flow for that host.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-02-28): Customer-facing incident page triggered. Notifying SRE and Oncall. Tentative P1 due to incident impact.
Marco Chen (2026-02-28): Reproduced on staging, confirmed rollback to v2.2.9 resolves the problem. Preparing emergency patch.
SRE (J. Nguyen) (2026-03-01): Deployed identity-proxy v2.3.1 to a 10% canary with patched cookie serializer; canary shows cookies Path='/' and runner flows succeed.
Oncall (L. Martínez) (2026-03-01): Using runner login --web as short-term workaround. Requesting timeline for full rollout and session invalidation guidance.
Marco Chen (2026-03-02): Hotfix PR merged and scheduled for full rollout; follow-up tasks include session invalidation broadcast and postmortem.
resolution:
Temporary workaround: instruct on-call to use 'runner login --web' or deploy identity-proxy to a local canary with REDWOOD_RUNNER_COOKIE_PATH=/ until patch is rolled out.
Permanent fix: revert the cookie-scoping change and update the serializer to avoid the 128-byte truncation; increase buffer and explicitly set Path='/' for SSO session cookies.
Action taken:
- PR #12912 merged to identity-proxy that fixes serializer and enforces Path='/' for SSO cookies.
- identity-proxy v2.3.1 rolled to prod canary 2026-03-01, full rollout completed 2026-03-02 03:10 UTC.
- Sessions: expired SSO cookies for affected hosts and forced a fresh login to ensure consistent cookie shape (communicated to staff via #oncall).
Follow-up / next steps:
- Postmortem to be drafted and linked to this ticket (owner: Marco Chen) due 2026-03-09.
- Add unit tests for cookie serializer and add integration test covering CLI elevation flows.
- Update runbook with guidance for cookie-path-related incidents and include a checklist for identity-proxy rollouts.
